patterns: The lever improves extraction completeness and accuracy in text regions, particularly for tabular data embedded in text (e.g., capturing all 15 rows in u-nrel-5mw-p25-36-5eaf02be-p10-text-b1of2) and reducing unsupported conditions (u-iea-15mw-p20-31-f7071680-p12-text).

In visual regions, the lever struggles because text often consists of labels, axis scales, or fragmented notes rather than prose. This leads to misreading scale multipliers as data values (u-iea-15mw-p20-31-f7071680-p7-text) or forcing pseudo-quotes from axis labels.

The lever sometimes causes the model to truncate values or drop valid conditions if they do not form a neat, contiguous quote (e.g., dropping the MDF material condition in u-calg-cd-p62-66-e0051bec-p5-table-b0of3).
tweaks: Relax or disable strict quote matching requirements for visual regions (plots, diagrams) where text primarily serves as labels or scale factors.
Allow for non-contiguous quotes or looser quote matching in tables and schedules to prevent the model from truncating valid values or conditions just to satisfy the quote constraint.
partitions: Text regions show strong performance (mean 0.773 across 22 units), indicating the lever is highly effective for prose.
Visual regions show poor performance (mean 0.444 across 9 units), as quote matching is less applicable to diagrams and plots.
Table regions have too little data (1 unit) to draw definitive statistical conclusions, though the single failure highlights truncation risks.
next: Run a round where the quote_match lever is applied exclusively to text regions, disabling it for visual and table regions.
Test a modification to the lever that explicitly instructs the model not to use axis scale multipliers as data values in plots.
note: The lever is highly beneficial for text but detrimental to visual data extraction where text is fragmented. Applying it conditionally based on region type should yield the best overall performance.
